title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
seo_title: Grade 10 Science: Chemical Reactions and Equations Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Evidence of chemical reactions; names and formulas; word and balanced chemical equations; types of chemical reactions; the law of conservation of mass. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 10, Quarter 3: Science of Materials)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Science of Materials): names and formulas, word and skeleton equations, balancing equations, types of reactions and conservation of mass. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mass is conserved: the atoms on each side of an equation must match.
key_sub: Synthesis, decomposition, single and double displacement.
body_html:
How to think about it

Name ionic compounds metal first, then the non-metal ending in -ide (sodium chloride, NaCl). Cross the ion charges to write formulas (Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃). Molecular compounds use prefixes: carbon dioxide (CO₂), dinitrogen tetroxide (N₂O₄).

A word equation names the substances; a skeleton equation uses formulas; a balanced equation adds coefficients so atoms are conserved. The four types are synthesis (A + B → AB), decomposition (AB → A + B), single displacement (A + BC → AC + B) and double displacement (AB + CD → AD + CB).

Example

Formula of calcium chloride?

Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻

Two Cl⁻ for each Ca²⁺

Answer: CaCl₂

Example

Balance: Na + Cl₂ → NaCl

2 Cl on the left, so 2 NaCl

Then 2 Na

Answer: 2Na + Cl₂ → 2NaCl

Common mistakes

  • Using prefixes for ionic compounds (it is calcium chloride, not calcium dichloride).
  • Changing subscripts to balance an equation.
  • Forgetting that oxygen, hydrogen and chlorine gases are diatomic.

faq.q: What is the law of conservation of mass?
faq.a: In a chemical reaction the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

faq.q: Why does a burning candle seem to lose mass?
faq.a: Gases (carbon dioxide and water vapor) escape into the air; in a closed container the mass stays the same.

items.q: What is the formula of lithium oxide?
items.e: Li<sup>+</sup> and O<sup>2−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is Li<sub>2</sub>O.

items.q: Al<sup>3+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup> ions combine. What is the formula of the compound?
items.e: Use the lowest numbers that make the total charge zero: 1 × (+3) + 3 × (−1) = 0.

items.q: What is the formula of potassium chloride?
items.e: K<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup>: the charges must balance, so the formula is KCl.

items.q: What is the name of BaCl<sub>2</sub>?
items.e: Name the metal, then the non-metal with -ide. Ionic names do not use prefixes.

items.q: Mae checks the equation for rusting of iron: 4Fe + 3O2 → 2Fe2O3. Is it balanced?
c: No. The reactants have more atoms.
Balance does not matter in reactions.
Yes. Each kind of atom has the same number on both sides.
No. The products have more atoms.
items.e: Atoms are only rearranged, so the counts match.

items.q: Rose's equation for magnesium burning is missing a coefficient: 2Mg + O2 → ?MgO. What number goes in place of the question mark?
items.e: With 2, every kind of atom has the same number on both sides.

items.q: Emmanuel's equation for making salt is missing a coefficient: 2Na + Cl2 → ?NaCl. What number goes in place of the question mark?
items.e: With 2, every kind of atom has the same number on both sides.

items.e: 2H<sub>2</sub>O: the coefficient 2 multiplies every atom in the formula, so 2 × 1 = 2.

items.q: Isabel's equation for methane burning is missing a coefficient: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + ?H2O. What number goes in place of the question mark?

c: Yes, because both sides have the same substances.
No. The number of some atoms is different on each side.
items.e: Count each kind of atom on both sides; at least one does not match.

items.q: Which general pattern matches 2H<sub>2</sub>O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O + O<sub>2</sub>?

items.q: Glucose (C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub>) burns completely in oxygen. What are the products?
items.e: Complete combustion of a compound of C and H (and O) gives CO₂ and H₂O.

items.q:

hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water
items.e: An acid and an alkali make a salt and water.

items.q: Barium reacts with sulfur. What is the formula of the product?

items.q: Marble chips react with acid in an open beaker on a balance. The mass shown goes down from 120 g to 118 g. Why?
c: Mass is destroyed in the reaction.
Carbon dioxide gas escapes into the air.
items.e: Mass is conserved; the gas leaves the beaker.

items.q: 96 g of copper is heated in air and reacts completely with 24 g of oxygen. What mass of copper(II) oxide is formed?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 96 + 24 = 120 g.

items.q: 15 g of magnesium burns in air and joins with 10 g of oxygen. What mass of magnesium oxide forms?
items.e: The magnesium gains the mass of the oxygen: 15 + 10.

items.q: Kevin heats 275 g of calcium carbonate in an open dish. It leaves 154 g of calcium oxide. What mass of carbon dioxide gas escaped?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 275 − 154 = 121 g of gas.
